<scxml xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2005/07/scxml" version="1.0" datamodel="ecmascript" initial="a">
  <datamodel><data id="d" expr="0"/></datamodel>
  <script>function keep(_event) { _event = 1; return _event; }</script>
  <state id="a">
    <onentry>
      <script>delete _event; _name += '!';</script>
      <script>Reflect.deleteProperty(globalThis, '_event'); delete globalThis._ioprocessors;</script>
      <assign location="d" expr="_sessionid = 'mine'"/>
    </onentry>
    <transition event="go" target="f"/>
  </state>
  <final id="f"/>
</scxml>

notes: SCXML 1.0 §5.10: "The Processor MUST cause any attempt to change the value of a system variable to fail and MUST place the error 'error.execution' on the internal event queue when such an attempt is made." The change fails at run time with `error.execution`; a non-strict `delete` or a reflective deletion through the global object returns `false` without one (a known limitation, docs/spec-errata.md). Variable names beginning with '_' are reserved for system use, and '_x' is the root of platform-specific system variables.
diagnostics.help: copy `_event` into a `<data>` variable and change that copy, or use a name that does not begin with `_`
